clue.text: In favour of model, one suggests

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a model is someone who poses for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone backing a fashion model puts forward an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposer is the person who puts forward a motion or idea at a meeting.

clue.text: Whoever wrote this dog's dinner must be round the bend!

indicators.note: something placed round another wraps it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: Pal is a well-known British brand of dog food
a U-bend is the curved pipe under a sink, so a bend is a U

explanation.surface: The setter cheerfully admits that anyone who produced such a mess of a puzzle must be mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter of this puzzle is Paul, so the definition points to his own name. 'Dog's dinner' (a mess) and 'round the bend' (mad) both look like idioms but are wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossword was compiled by the setter Paul, whose pseudonym appears with the grid.

clue.text: Sweet Baby puts singer on the dole

parts.note: Cher is the American pop singer
UB is unemployment benefit, money paid to someone on the dole

explanation.surface: A baby (perhaps a pop star's lover) sends a singer off to claim unemployment money.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is British slang for state unemployment pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is an angelic child, so a sweet, chubby-faced baby is called one.

clue.text: Country teacher promoted by University? Yes!

indicators.note: in a down clue being promoted moves a word upward, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university
a guru is a spiritual teacher
ay is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher gets promoted to a university post and celebrates.
explanation.definitionFit: Uruguay is a South American nation lying between Argentina and Brazil.

clue.text: Boxer getting beaten up? So what!

indicators.note: beaten things are knocked about and battered out of shape, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A boxer shrugs off a beating with a defiant 'so what?'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten up' reads as a phrase, but 'up' belongs with 'so what' as the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw is a left-handed fighter, so the word names a type of boxer.

clue.text: Vulgar words recur with naval orders

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so the letters are put into a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sailors' commands are full of swearing that keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: Vulgar here has its old sense of common or of the people, not rude.
explanation.definitionFit: The vernacular is the everyday spoken language of ordinary people, the old sense of vulgar tongue.

clue.text: Producer of music by wartime singer is heard

indicators.note: something heard is taken in by ear, so the spoken sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: Vera Lynn was the British forces' sweetheart of the Second World War

explanation.surface: A wartime song is played to the troops by a famous singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly in a British accent, Dame Vera Lynn's name comes close to the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A violin is a stringed instrument, something that produces music when played.

clue.text: Short break for the tired heart, you might say?

definitions.text: Short break for the tired heart, you might say?

parts.note: surface reading: a brief rest from work

parts.words: for the tired heart, you might say
parts.note: setter's reading: an overworked heart that keeps the lungs going would welcome a pause to recover

explanation.walkthrough: A pounding, exhausted heart is pictured as needing time off; 'you might say' flags that the clue is a playful description, not a dictionary entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A breather is a short pause for rest, a chance to get your breath back.

clue.text: Former pupil and priest, daggers drawn

parts.note: an old boy, OB, is a former pupil of a school
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: An old schoolboy and a clergyman are at daggers drawn, openly hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At daggers drawn' is an idiom for open hostility; here the daggers are drawn with a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are the dagger-shaped printers' marks used for footnotes, symbols that are written or printed.

clue.text: Stone circles rolled over

indicators.note: something rolled over is turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a lap is a circuit and an O is a ring shape, two circles

explanation.surface: A stone circle, like Stonehenge, has its stones toppled.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal is a gemstone, prized for its iridescent play of colour.

clue.text: Set up hot network at proper meeting place

parts.note: to rig is to set up, as with equipment or a ship's sails
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
a tangle is a mesh or web of twisted strands

explanation.surface: A spy sets up a hot network at the agreed rendezvous.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: two lines meeting squarely meet at a 'proper' angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A right angle is where two perpendicular lines meet, so 'right' supplies proper and the corner is a meeting point.

clue.text: See 22 down

definitions.note: the definition, a tart past its sell-by date, is in the clue at 22 down

wordplay.note: an instruction to read the numbered clue, which builds the whole phrase this light ends

explanation.walkthrough: This light is the end of MUTTON DRESSED AS LAMB, clued at 22 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Together with the lights at 22 down and 15 it spells the idiom for an older woman wearing styles meant for the young.

clue.text: Fortunate to see a dodgy leader dismissed

indicators.note: dismissing a leader sends away the one at the front, so the opening letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
something dodgy looks suspicious

explanation.surface: It is a relief to watch a shady boss being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Dodgy is British slang for shady or untrustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Auspicious means favourable or promising good luck, so circumstances that are auspicious are fortunate.

clue.text: Actor and llama's relative almost totally in love

indicators.note: almost totally means everything but a tiny bit, so the final letter is left off

parts.note: the alpaca is a South American cousin of the llama
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An actor and a llama's cousin are almost completely besotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Pacino is the American film star of The Godfather and Scarface.

clue.text: See 22 down

definitions.note: the definition, a tart past its sell-by date, is in the clue at 22 down

wordplay.note: an instruction to read the numbered clue, which builds the whole phrase this light belongs to

explanation.walkthrough: This light is the middle of MUTTON DRESSED AS LAMB, clued at 22 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Together with the lights at 22 down and 12 it spells the idiom for an older woman wearing styles meant for the young.

clue.text: Subject of musical opera never missing Royal Performance

indicators.note: a performance puts on a new show, so the remaining letters are staged in a fresh order
words that are missing something have had letters taken out of them

parts.note: taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of the Queen

explanation.surface: The heroine of a musical never appears in an opera at a Royal Command Performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ER out of 'opera never' to leave OPA NEVER, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva Perón, wife of the Argentine president, is the central figure of Lloyd Webber's musical Evita.

clue.text: (and 21, 26) Voracity 15 12?

parts.note: surface reading: greed or ravenous appetite
setter's reading: the cross-references read as a phrase about disguise, so a ravenous beast is disguised as a young sheep

explanation.walkthrough: 15 and 12 together give 'dressed as lamb', from the companion clue at 22 down; the greedy animal is the one famous for its voracity.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a dangerous person hiding behind a harmless appearance, like the greedy predator in Aesop's fable.

clue.text: Shame in my going topless? Shameful!

indicators.note: topless means without a top, so the word going loses its first letter
something shameful is disgraceful and out of order, so the letters end in a jumble

parts.note: taken as written
the word with its first letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone frets about the disgrace of going about topless.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignominy is public disgrace or humiliation, a close synonym for the noun shame.

clue.text: Distort time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pull out of shape
second meaning: a period served in prison

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like science fiction about warping time, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch something warps it out of shape, and a stretch is slang for a prison sentence.

clue.text: Pretender wants partisan exposed

indicators.note: something exposed is laid open and pulled apart, so the letters are reset in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A claimant to the throne wants an enemy guerrilla unmasked.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone with ambitions to a position, as a pretender lays claim to a throne.

clue.text: See 17

definitions.note: the definition, voracity dressed as lamb, is in the clue at 17

wordplay.note: an instruction to read the numbered clue, which builds the whole phrase this light belongs to

explanation.walkthrough: This light is the middle of A WOLF IN SHEEP'S CLOTHING, clued at 17.
explanation.definitionFit: Together with the lights at 17 and 26 it spells the idiom for a menacing person hiding behind a harmless appearance.

clue.text: River enters the sea at a harbour

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea
R is the abbreviation for river on maps
taken as written

explanation.surface: A river flows into the sea beside a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a small harbour with moorings for yachts and pleasure boats.

clue.text: (and 15, 12) Meat tart past its sell-by date?

definitions.text: Meat tart past its sell-by date?

parts.words: Meat tart past its sell-by date
parts.note: surface reading: a stale meat pastry that has gone off
setter's reading: an older woman (tart in its slang sense) dressing far too young for her years

explanation.walkthrough: Tart looks like a pastry, but it is slang for a woman; the meat is an old sheep made up as a young one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom mocks an older woman wearing clothes styled for someone much younger; the meat of an old sheep is sold as young.

clue.text: Concerned with flag, soldiers last to effect withdrawal

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to flag is to grow weary
soldiers are men of the ranks

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only the end letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of effect

explanation.surface: Troops under a flag finally carry out a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag is a verb here, meaning tire, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Retirement is a withdrawal, whether from work or an army pulling back from the field.

clue.text: All round sport!

parts.note: the sum is the whole amount, all of it
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising an all-round sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All round' looks like one phrase, but the words are separate pieces; round is also a nod to the wrestlers' build.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the Japanese form of heavyweight wrestling, a traditional sport.

clue.text: Part of central London, then little accommodation?

parts.note: so means then or therefore
ho is the short form of house

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether there is little housing in central London.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a district of London's West End, known for its nightlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district in the West End, in the heart of the British capital.

clue.text: Heavenly body is hell

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an object in the solar system
second meaning: the god of the underworld, standing for the underworld itself

explanation.walkthrough: Heaven and hell sit side by side in the surface; one word is both the distant planet and the Roman underworld god.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto was then counted the ninth planet, and the Roman ruler of the dead gave his name to the underworld.

clue.text: See 17

definitions.note: the definition, voracity dressed as lamb, is in the clue at 17

wordplay.note: an instruction to read the numbered clue, which builds the whole phrase this light ends

explanation.walkthrough: This light is the end of A WOLF IN SHEEP'S CLOTHING, clued at 17.
explanation.definitionFit: Together with the lights at 17 and 21 it spells the idiom for a menacing person hiding behind a harmless appearance.
